questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: What is the configuration of a chiral center whose lowest-priority group points away and whose 1-to-2-to-3 order runs clockwise?

options.text: S, with the lowest group pointing away
options.misconception: reverses the clockwise convention

options.text: R, with the lowest group pointing away
The center is achiral and has no descriptor
options.misconception: mistakes four different groups for a mirror plane

options.text: E, because groups straddle a double bond
options.misconception: confuses R/S with alkene E/Z notation

questions.explanation: With the lowest-priority group directed away, a clockwise 1-2-3 sequence is assigned R; viewing from the opposite side would invert the descriptor.
questions.hint: Point the lowest group away, then read one to two to three.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Identify the most stable chair conformation
questions.stem: When analyzing the transformation, which conformation places a bulky tert-butyl group in an equatorial position?

options.misconception: boats are higher in energy than chairs
overlooks severe 1,3-diaxial strain
doubly destabilizes the conformation

questions.explanation: A chair places substituents in equatorial sites where 1,3-diaxial interactions are avoided, and a tert-butyl group has a very strong equatorial preference.
questions.hint: Bulky groups prefer equatorial sites in a chair.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Rank acids by conjugate base stability
questions.stem: In a tutorial session, which feature most strongly stabilizes a conjugate base and raises the acidity of its parent acid?

options.text: A longer alkyl chain at the acidic site
options.misconception: alkyl groups destabilize anions by induction

options.text: A greater number of alkyl substituents
options.misconception: electron donation raises the pKa

options.text: More steric bulk around the acidic proton
options.misconception: sterics do not stabilize the anion

options.text: Resonance delocalization of the negative charge

questions.explanation: Acidity rises when the conjugate base is stabilized, most effectively by resonance or electron-withdrawing induction, both of which lower the pKa.
questions.hint: Think about what stabilizes the anion formed.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Classify a reagent by electronic role
questions.stem: You are given the following: what role does a species bearing a lone pair and a negative charge usually play in a polar reaction?

options.misconception: confuses electron donors with acceptors
a lone-pair donor is a Lewis base
ignores the drive to neutralize charge

questions.explanation: A negatively charged species with available electrons donates them to an electron-poor center, which is exactly the definition of a nucleophile.
questions.hint: Electron-rich species seek electron-poor partners.

questions.stem: In a synthesis planning session, which statement about two valid resonance contributors of a carboxylate ion is correct?

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A laboratory report asks: which condition must a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated ring meet to be aromatic?

options.text: It must contain exactly 4n pi electrons
options.misconception: planar 4n systems are antiaromatic

options.text: It must contain an odd number of pi electrons
options.misconception: an odd count leaves an unpaired electron

options.misconception: a single ring can be aromatic
